newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa hits 19-week low on spec sell-off.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa hits 19-week low on spec sell-off.

text.p: Widespread speculative liquidation hammered LIFFE cocoa futures to the lowest level in 19 weeks on Monday with benchmark September losing 2.7 percent on the day, traders said.
"It was general spec liquidation. But where we go from here is difficult to say. We will see whether the spec selling is finished," said one trader.
Volume was brisk at 7,744 lots and nearby switches widened considerably as rampant selling emerged at the outset.
Benchmark September, the day's most active position, finished midsession at 988 stg a tonne for a steep 27 stg loss.
It had broken the psychologically-important 1,000 stg support in the first 25 minutes of trading, and then tested the 988 stg low after filling a chart gap at 989-1,010 left since March 11.
Sept/Dec spread widened to a high of 40 stg from 32 at Friday's close.
Traders had expected a large retracement if the 1,000 stg support gave way. The test on the downside was also expected since the contract finished at its lows on Friday.
The next key support is pegged at 950 stg, a level not seen since March 6, this year.
Resistance is now seen at 1,000 stg and then last week's high of 1,052 followed by the 1,063 peak notched up just after the breakaway slide at the start of the month.
Cocoa's technical picture looked more promising until the major setback on July 3 when prices lost more than 100 stg on one day alone.
The market had peaked at 1,170 two days earlier before the speculative sell-off set in.
On the fundamental front, even the rosy second-quarter U.S. grind data released on Friday and coming after a lacklustre European figures failed to encourage the buyers.

The U.S. CFTC Commitment of Traders released late on Friday showed that while the fund long positions had been reduced by around 6,000 lots, the funds remained very long of New York cocoa, broker GNI said.
